confirmed_gaps.root_cause: unary_call_lowering.py:346-363 only matches str.maketrans with len(expr.args)==2; the 3-arg delete form (str.maketrans(x,y,z)) has no native branch, so it falls through to the libpython fallback. The C/port runtime py_str_maketrans is 2-arg only (py_str_accessors.c:1250 comment explicitly says '3-arg delete forms are follow-ons'). A new runtime helper py_str_maketrans3(x,y,z) is needed plus a 3-arg frontend branch.

proposed_edits.note: Declare the 3-arg maketrans runtime ABI: (x, y, z) -> dict, returns PyObject*.

confirmed_gaps.root_cause: string_method_lowering.py has two rsplit branches (lines 319 and 754) both gated on `1 <= len(expr.args) <= 2`. The 0-arg whitespace form (rsplit()) is excluded and falls through to libpython. Without a maxsplit limit, rsplit() over whitespace yields the exact same parts in the same order as split() (verified: both give ['x','y','z']), so it can route to py_str_split with a NULL sep exactly like the 0-arg split branch does (lines 305-306, 314-317).

proposed_edits.note: Dyn-receiver rsplit site (~line 319). Accept 0 args and route the whitespace form to py_str_split with NULL sep, mirroring the 0-arg split path. _CSTR and ir are already imported in this module (used by the split branch at lines 305-306).

Static-str rsplit site (~line 754). Same 0-arg whitespace handling. Note this only fixes rsplit() (no args); rsplit(None, n) whitespace-with-limit is intentionally left to fall back (order-from-right with a limit differs from split and would need py_str_rsplit_maxsplit to accept a NULL sep).

confirmed_gaps.root_cause: py_str_join only accepts PY_TYPE_LIST. C: py_str_accessors.c:1503 `py_type_of(list) != PY_TYPE_LIST` -> returns NULL for a tuple (PY_TYPE_TUPLE=7). Port mirror: py_str_accessors.py:1974 `_type_of(lst) != 5` -> null(). The frontend lowering (string_method_lowering.py:399 / 835) correctly passes the tuple object; the gap is runtime-only. str.join over a list works; over a tuple it silently returns NULL. Tuple layout differs from list: tuple has len at offset 16 and INLINE items[] at offset 24 (flexible array), while list has length at 16 and an items POINTER at offset 32. Fix: accept tag 7 and read items from the inline base (offset 24) for tuples.

proposed_edits.note: Accept both PY_TYPE_LIST and PY_TYPE_TUPLE. Branch the slot address: tuple items are inline (&((PyTupleObject*)list)->items[i]), list items via the items pointer (&((PyListObject*)list)->items[i]). PyTupleObject is visible (py_str_accessors.c includes py_internal.h). Both slot reads go through pcc_gc_load_ptr(list, slot) so GC relocation barriers stay correct for both.

Port mirror. Accept tuple tag 7; tuple len shares offset 16 with list length. For a tuple, items base is the inline array at offset 24 so the existing `ptr_add(items, i*8)` slot math in both loops works unchanged. ptr_add is already used in this function (out_data = ptr_add(out, 40)).

The runtime py_str_count (py_str_accessors.c:837) is 2-arg (s, sub) only and has no start/end variant. A new runtime helper py_str_count_range(s, sub, start, end) with CPython-style index normalization (negative -> +len, clamp to [0,len]) is needed plus a frontend branch for the 2-/3-arg forms. NOTE: pcc str helpers are byte-oriented; start/end are byte indices (matches CPython for ASCII; differs for multi-byte UTF-8, same limitation as the rest of the str helper family).

confirmed_gaps.idiom: "a b c d".rsplit(None, 2)   # whitespace rsplit WITH a maxsplit limit
confirmed_gaps.observed: ['a b c d']  (whole string returned, no split)
confirmed_gaps.expected: ['a b', 'c', 'd']  (CPython: split from the right on whitespace, at most 2 splits; head keeps internal whitespace)
confirmed_gaps.root_cause: py_str_rsplit_maxsplit (py_str_accessors.c:1071 / port py_str_accessors.py:1439) never checks whether sep is None/py_None. The frontend rsplit branch (string_method_lowering.py:319/754) marshals the literal None into the py_None object and calls py_str_rsplit_maxsplit(recv, py_None, maxsplit). The runtime blindly casts sep to PyStrObject* and reads sp->byte_len at offset 16 of the None object (undefined; here nonzero), so no separator ever matches and the whole string is returned. The forward path is correct -- py_str_split_maxsplit checks `sep == NULL || sep == py_None` and routes to py_str_split_whitespace_maxsplit (line 1431-1464). rsplit needs the analogous guard plus a right-to-right whitespace+limit helper (rsplit(None,n) differs from split(None,n): keeps the LAST n tokens separate, lumps the rest into the head substring preserving its internal whitespace).

proposed_edits.note: Add a None/py_None guard to py_str_rsplit_maxsplit that routes to a new static py_str_rsplit_whitespace_maxsplit, defined just above. strip_is_ascii_ws and py_str_split_whitespace are existing statics in this TU (used by the forward whitespace splitters at lines 919/1390). VERIFY edge cases against CPython with the regression: 'a  b c d'.rsplit(None,2)==['a  b','c','d']; '   x y z   '.rsplit(None,1)==['   x y','z']; 'oneword'.rsplit(None,2)==['oneword']; '   '.rsplit(None,2)==[]; 'a b'.rsplit(None,5)==['a','b']. The head_end==0 case (all-leading-ws or empty head) correctly emits no head element.
